newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland Bank gov sees no risk of overheating.
newsitem.headline: Finland Bank gov sees no risk of overheating.

text.p: Bank of Finland governor Sirkka Hamalainen said on Wednesday that despite strong growth she saw no risk that the Finnish economy would overheat this year, as not all its capacity was fully used.
"I do not fear overheating, as capacity is not fully used," she told a news conference.

"We are in a positive situation, in that we have strong growth and no inflation pressures in sight," she said at a conference with the publication of the bank's quarterly economic review, Markka ja Talous.

She declined to comment on some views that Finland may be losing scope to conduct independent monetary policy in the run-up to European economic and monetary union (EMU), saying the central bank's policy decisions were based on inflation prospects and exchange rate stability.
"In the medium term, exchange rate stability and inflation targets are in balance," she added.
She also cited low inflation to say she did not see why nominal wages should rise in a national round of incomes talks due this autumn.

"On the domestic front, the incomes agreement is crucial and I do not see any reason why there should be (any) wage increases with this inflation outlook," she said, referring to the bank's view that 1997 core inflation would stay within the two percent target.
